SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: Acute shortness of breath, right-sided pleuritic back pain on deep inspiration, hemoptysis (coughed up blood twice), subjective fever, awareness of heartbeat, fatigue with reduced exercise tolerance and difficulty performing daily activities.
- Onset/duration: Acute respiratory symptoms began today; fatigue present ~2 weeks.
- Past medical history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
- Past surgeries: Not documented.
- Medications:
  • Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented (last dose taken this morning).
- Social history:
  • Non-smoker.
  • Desk-based office job.
  • Lives alone in a flat; owns a cat.
  • No recent long-haul flights; no personal or family history of venous thromboembolism.
- Allergies: Denies medication or other allergies.

Objective:
- Remote exam findings:
  • Self-counted radial pulse: 11–12 beats/10 s ≈ 66–72 bpm, regular.
  • Capillary refill brisk (<2 s) on fingertip.
  • Oropharynx visualized via phone camera – no abnormalities reported by clinician.
  • Patient-palpated cervical lymph nodes: no enlargement.
- No other vitals (temperature, BP, RR, SpO₂) or in-person chest/respiratory exam performed.
- Investigations: None performed yet.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough with hemoptysis / pleuritic chest pain
   - Assessment: Likely lower respiratory tract infection / pneumonia.
   - Differential diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism, pleurisy, malignancy (lung cancer), lupus-related pulmonary involvement.
   - Investigations planned:
     • In-person assessment today for auscultation, BP, pulse, temperature.
     • Consider chest X-ray and/or further imaging if examination abnormal or poor response to treatment.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Empirical oral antibiotic likely after clinical assessment (specific agent to be decided).
   - Relevant referrals:
     • Same-day face-to-face GP clinic appointment arranged via support team.

2. Fatigue
   - Assessment: Possibly secondary to current infection; also consider methotrexate effect or SLE activity.
   - Investigations planned: Review once acute issue resolved; consider CBC and inflammatory markers if persists.
   - Treatment planned: Address underlying cause; no specific therapy today.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements:
  – Objective vitals (temperature, BP, RR, SpO₂).
  – Full medication list with dosages.
  – Detailed SLE history and current disease control.
  – Recent methotrexate monitoring labs.

• Internal conflicts:
  – Patient gave two different names (“Tracy Chapman” vs “Doris”) – conflict noted.
  – Age stated as 45; exact DOB not provided.

• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional name confusion and minor inaudible gaps; remote exam inherently limited.
